sections.h2: Where is Carroll County, Iowa, and how is it laid out?
sections.html:
Carroll County sits in west central Iowa and covers about 570 square miles, almost all of it land. Carroll is the county seat, and the county shares borders with Sac, Calhoun, Greene, Guthrie, Audubon and Crawford counties.

The 2020 census counted 20,760 residents. Roughly half of them live in the city of Carroll, which had 10,321 people. The next largest places are small: Manning (1,455), Coon Rapids (1,300, partly in Guthrie County), Glidden (1,151), Arcadia (525) and Breda (500). Smaller towns include Templeton, Halbur, Dedham, Lidderdale, Lanesboro, Ralston and Willey.

sections.h2: How has Carroll County changed over time?
sections.html:
Carroll County was formed on January 15, 1851, from part of Pottawattamie County, and it is named for Charles Carroll of Carrollton, a signer of the Declaration of Independence. County government began at Carrollton in 1855, and the seat moved to the railroad town of Carroll City in 1869 after a vote.

A courthouse fire in 1886 destroyed the building on the town square. The courthouse in use today dates from the mid 1960s and houses the treasurer and the assessor at 114 E. 6th Street.

Population peaked a few decades ago and has eased since. The table below uses decennial census figures and the latest estimate.

sections.h2: What is Carroll like for a homeowner: climate, schools and employers?
sections.html:
The city of Carroll has a humid continental climate with about 33.7 inches of precipitation and about 29 inches of snow in an average year.

Public schools in the city belong to the Carroll Community School District, and the Kuemper Catholic School System, including Kuemper Catholic High School, is the private option.

St. Anthony Regional Hospital is based on South Clark Street. The latest county business statistics we found are from the 2002 Economic Census, so treat them as history: health care, retail, wholesale trade and manufacturing were the biggest employment sectors. The city's own economic development page says it works with the Carroll Area Development Corporation to make Carroll a regional business center for west central Iowa.

sections.h2: Who handles property tax in Carroll County?
sections.html:
Three jobs are split between offices: the assessor sets value, the auditor builds the bill from local budgets, and the treasurer collects the money. Iowa's Department of Revenue describes the same split statewide, with more than 2,000 levying authorities sharing the proceeds.

  • Carroll County Treasurer: 114 E. 6th Street, first floor of the courthouse, Carroll, IA 51401. Phone 712-792-1200. Handles payments, delinquent taxes and the tax sale.
  • Carroll County Assessor: in the same courthouse. The assessor is Sarah Haberl. The county site lists 712-792-9973 in one notice and another number in a closure notice, so call before you drive over.
  • Board of Review: hears protests each spring. Petitions go through the assessor's office.
  • Iowa Department of Revenue: sets statewide rules and orders equalization between classes of property.

sections.h2: What is the Carroll County reappraisal, and when do new values start?
sections.html:
Carroll County is in the middle of a full reappraisal that finishes December 31, 2026, with new values taking effect January 1, 2027. The Conference Board approved the project in February 2022, and the county is working with Vanguard Appraisals.

Appraisers collect construction type, interior finish, condition, age and exterior measurements, and they do not give a value at the door. Final value notices go out after January 1, 2027, and informal meetings are planned for spring 2027. The assessor says the new values apply to taxes payable in fiscal 2028 and 2029.

If you plan to sell in the next year, this is worth knowing. Your current tax bill reflects the old valuation, and a buyer who sees a low bill today may face a higher one after the 2027 notices. Appraisers cite Iowa Code section 441.17 for the right to enter property for assessment. They knock before exterior work, leave if you ask, and need your permission for interior walk-throughs of new construction.

sections.h2: When are Carroll County property taxes due, and what happens if they are late?
sections.html:
Iowa property tax is paid in two halves, with the first half due September 1 and the second half due March 1. Interest starts the next month, October 1 for the first half and April 1 for the second, at 1.5 percent per month, with weekend rules that can move the cutoff a day or two.

ItemDate or rule
First half dueSeptember 1, payable through September 30
Second half dueMarch 1, payable through March 31
Late interest1.5% per month, rounded to the nearest dollar, $1 minimum
Mailed paymentsMust be postmarked before the delinquent date
Tax sale interest for the buyer2% per month on the sale amount

Under Iowa Code 445.37, a payment that is not made electronically has to reach the treasurer by the last business day before the delinquent month, or be postmarked in time. Statements go to the titleholder of record even when a mortgage lender pays from escrow.

sections.h2: How does the Carroll County tax sale work?
sections.html:
Carroll County sells unpaid taxes once a year, on the third Monday in June, and the 2026 sale ran on June 15 online through GovEase, with bidding from 9:00 to 10:30 a.m. Bidders had to register between May 18 and June 11 and pay a $40 registration fee.

Bidding starts at 100 percent and moves down in whole percentages. The lowest percentage wins, and ties go to a random draw. The winner pays the delinquent taxes, interest and a $20 certificate fee, and the owner keeps the right to redeem by paying the sale amount plus 2 percent per month.

  • A 90-day redemption notice can be served after one year and nine months on a regular sale.
  • On a public bidder parcel, advertised for two years, the notice can be served after nine months.
  • The redemption amount can include a record search cost of up to $300, plus service and publication costs.
  • The delinquent list is published in the Carroll Times Herald in late May.

sections.h2: How do you protest a Carroll County assessment?
sections.html:
File a written petition with the Board of Review between April 2 and April 30 of the assessment year. The existing county listing says the same, and the board cannot extend the window.

The grounds under Iowa Code 441.37 are that the assessment is not equitable compared with like property, that it exceeds the legal value, that the property is exempt or misclassified, that there is an error, or that there is fraud. Petition forms are available from the assessor's office, and the Property Assessment Appeal Board explains the process on its own site.

In years when the state issues an equalization order that raises your class, a second short protest window runs from October 9 to October 31, and the only argument allowed is that the order pushed your value above what Iowa Code 441.21 permits. A decision can be appealed to the Property Assessment Appeal Board or to district court within 20 days after the board adjourns.

sections.h2: What does the new Iowa homestead exemption mean for a Carroll County seller?
sections.html:
Iowa replaced the homestead tax credit with a homestead exemption under SF 2472, signed May 18, 2026, and it applies from assessment year 2026. The exemption is 10 percent of the home's taxable value, with a floor of $5,500 and a ceiling of $20,000 of taxable value, and it first reaches bills paid in September 2027 and March 2028.

The Department of Revenue says current claimants do not need to refile.

sections.h2: What city incentives affect the value of a Carroll house?
sections.html:
The city of Carroll runs an urban revitalization area that offers a five year exemption on the first $75,000 of added value from improvements. Construction has to follow February 25, 2019 in the original area, or November 22, 2021 in the expanded area, and the project must raise assessed value by at least 10 percent.

The city also lists an Infill Housing Incentive of $20,000 per new owner-occupied home while funds last, and a speculative home loan program backed by five local banks. These programs favor new construction, so an older house competes with new homes that carry abatements and incentive money.

sections.h2: What happens to property tax when you sell a Carroll County house?
sections.html:
In a normal sale, the seller's share of the current tax is credited to the buyer at closing. The Iowa Treasurers' site says taxes are prorated and that the closing statement shows the split.

Iowa also charges a transfer tax of 80 cents for each $500 of value above the first $500, under Iowa Code 428A.1. A declaration of value, signed by at least one seller or buyer, goes in with every deed, and the recorder forwards it to the assessor, who keeps it three years. The statute does not say which party pays the tax, so the purchase contract decides that.

Unpaid city charges such as water or sewer that have been certified to the treasurer become a lien with the same priority as ordinary tax. They have to be cleared at closing.

faqs.q: When are property taxes due in Carroll County, Iowa?
faqs.a: The first half is due September 1 and the second half is due March 1. Interest begins October 1 and April 1 at 1.5 percent per month, and weekend dates can shift the cutoff.

faqs.q: Where do I pay Carroll County property tax?
faqs.a: Pay at the Carroll County Treasurer on the first floor of the courthouse, 114 E. 6th Street, Carroll, or call 712-792-1200. The Iowa Treasurers' site also takes online payments, with a fee for cards and e-checks.

faqs.q: When can I protest my Carroll County assessment?
faqs.a: You can file between April 2 and April 30 of the assessment year with the Board of Review. A second window from October 9 to October 31 applies only when a state equalization order raises your value.

faqs.q: Will my Carroll County property tax change after the reappraisal?
faqs.a: It can. New values take effect January 1, 2027, and the assessor expects them to apply to taxes payable in fiscal 2028 and 2029. Notices come after January 1, 2027.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Carroll County house that has back taxes?
faqs.a: Yes. Back taxes and interest are paid from the sale proceeds at closing. If the taxes have already been sold at the June tax sale, the redemption amount, which includes 2 percent per month, has to be paid too.
